High GC activity can cause pauses and slow down applications, leading to increased response times.

These are response time metrics, which would be affected if the backend databases or Tomcats are slow. Also, Redis01 has high CPU utilization, reaching 74.58% at one point. High CPU use could affect performance, but the main issue seems to be with the Tomcats and Mysql. Or perhaps it's a different metric. Alternatively, the Mysql01's disk busy is a big red flag.

Putting this together: The highest priority is probably the Tomcat instances because they're directly experiencing memory issues leading to GC, which affects their ability to process requests. Then, the Mysql01's disk being busy could be contributing to slower queries, which in turn makes the Tomcats work harder. Finally, the high disk writes on MG01 might be part of the same issue, possibly due to the Tomcats writing a lot of data, but that's less direct.

Wait, the reference case had Mysql02 as the root cause because of disk and transaction issues. In this case, Mysql01's disk is very busy. But also, the Tomcats are having memory issues. Which is more critical?

Alternatively, the high GC events in Tomcat02, 03, 04 could be the root cause. Because if the apps are constantly getting GCed, that leads to high response times.
